messages:
anita: Canary finished for the reserve-short-path + deficit-credit changes. Quick win on short-tenant tails, but small throughput regression for heavy long-workloads.
mike: can you paste the numbers?
anita: perf-bot summary below. TL;DR: short p95 improved ~3.7x vs baseline, short p99 down ~2.5x; long throughput -6%. CPU/GPU steady.
perf-bot: run: cbatch/canary-2026-03-18
perf-bot: config: queue_policy=weighted-fair, reserve_short_tokens_pct=6, short_seq_threshold=48, tenant_credit_mode=adaptive, max_batch_tokens=4096
perf-bot: short-tenant p95: 140ms (baseline 520ms)
perf-bot: short-tenant p99: 320ms (baseline 800ms)
perf-bot: long-tenant throughput: -6% vs baseline
perf-bot: GPU util: 91% (baseline 93%)
ravi: promising. walk me through the heuristic again? how do credits work with batch formation?
anita: high level: each tenant has a token credit balance replenished per second. short requests (<48) consume small credit amounts and can be admitted into a reserved short bucket per batch. if tenant balance insufficient, request goes to best-effort. unused reserved tokens roll back to general pool at batch close.
olga: kernel selection note: runtime currently selects kernel based on measured amortized throughput for a batch. mixed batches with many long sequences bias kernel choice toward long-optimized codepaths -> increases head-of-line for short requests.
lee: sketch of the policy we tested:
```json
{
  "queue_policy": "weighted-fair",
  "reserve_short_tokens_pct": 6,
  "short_seq_threshold": 48,
  "tenant_credit_policy": "adaptive",
  "tenant_credit_formula": "min(max(256, ceil(0.01 * tenant_rps * avg_seq_len)), 4096)",
  "kernel_bias_for_mixed_batches": { "short_preference_threshold": 0.3, "short_kernel_delta_tolerance_pct": 8 }
}
```
mike: two thoughts: 1) we should cap the reserve so it can't starve big tenants (config above looks ok). 2) add metric surfaces and an alert if reserved_short_utilization > 90% for >5m.
ravi: agree. add dashboards: tenant_credit_balance_percentiles, short_bucket_head_time_p95, mixed_batch_kernel_switch_count.
anita: one observed blocked trace for reference:
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] incoming tenant=svc-A seq_len=16
[queue] queued in short bucket (balance>=cost) -> admitted into batch 412
[batcher] batch 412 preempted long-only batch 411, total_tokens=512, short_tokens=48
[completion] short req p95=132ms
```
lee: kernel bias idea: when short_fraction_in_batch >= short_preference_threshold, prefer short-optimized kernels even if they give slightly lower throughput per-GPU; reduces short-tail significantly. I have a PoC in my branch.
olga: need safety: only apply kernel bias if mixed_batch_kernel_switch_count < 100/min to avoid oscillation.
mike: also add a perf-gate in CI: on canary runs assert that short_p95 <= baseline * 2 and long_throughput >= baseline - 10%. fail the job if violated.
anita: timeline: lee will open PR today (target review by EOD), we run canary deploy 09:00 PT tomorrow, perf harness run and gating tests, dashboards added by ravi.
lee: will do PR and include feature flags: reserve_short_tokens and kernel_bias.
ravi: i'll add dashboards and the alert rule.
anita: thanks team. i'll monitor canary and post updates. :thumbsup:
